title: The refund agent saw too much
scenario: An online shop runs customer support on the OpenAI Agents SDK. A triage agent talks to the customer first and can hand off to specialists. Before any handoff, triage runs a fraud-check tool whose output holds internal risk notes. You review the setup and one trace (exhibit). The shop, the trace and the data are made up for this case.
exhibit:
SETUP (made up for this case)
  triage agent
    tools:     fraud_check
    handoffs:  billing agent, refund agent, FAQ agent
  input_filter: none

TRACE 2026-10-02 (made up)
  user:        I was charged twice for order 5521.
  triage:      fraud_check(order=5521)
  tool result: risk=low; note="customer flagged in 2024 chargeback dispute"
  triage:      transfer_to_refund_agent
  refund:      I can see a note about a 2024 dispute...

OPEN REQUESTS
- Product: when the customer replies after a refund answer, the refund agent should answer again.
- Ops: log WHY each refund handoff happened, and how urgent it is.
- Security: we move to server-managed history (previous_response_id). The input_filter fix must still work.

questions.prompt: Product wants the next customer message to go straight back to the refund agent. What does the OpenAI results guide suggest?

options.text: Start every turn at triage and tell it to prefer refunds.
options.explanation: That repeats routing each turn and relies on a prompt. The guide names a result field for this.

options.text: Reuse `last_agent` from the result as the agent for the next turn.
options.explanation: Right. The results guide says to reuse `last_agent` after handoffs when that specialist should stay in control next turn.

options.text: Have triage call the refund agent with `as_tool` on the next turn.
options.explanation: With agents as tools the manager keeps the reply, so triage would own it, not the refund agent.

options.text: Disable the billing and FAQ handoffs with `is_enabled`.
options.explanation: `is_enabled` decides which handoffs exist. It does not keep the refund agent active for the next turn.

questions.prompt: The refund agent quoted the internal risk note. Why did it see the note, and what is the fix?

options.text: The handoff description was too long, so the model chose it; shorten it.
options.explanation: The description helps the model choose a handoff. It does not control what history the next agent receives.

options.text: The refund agent has `is_enabled` set to true; set it to false instead.
options.explanation: `is_enabled` turns the handoff on or off. Setting it to false would stop refunds, not hide the note.

options.text: Add an `input_type` schema to the handoff so that the note is replaced.
options.explanation: The docs say `input_type` does not replace the next agent's main input. The receiving agent still sees the history.

options.text: By default it sees the whole history; add an `input_filter`.
options.explanation: Right. The docs say the new agent sees the entire history unless an `input_filter` changes it. `remove_all_tools` removes tool items but not text copied into messages, so check what is left.

questions.prompt: Ops wants a reason and a priority recorded at the moment of each refund handoff. What fits the SDK docs?

options.text: Set an `input_type` with reason and priority; log them in `on_handoff`.
options.explanation: Right. The docs use this exact case: the model sends metadata like `reason` and `priority`, and `on_handoff` can log it before the refund agent takes over.

options.text: Store reason and priority in the run context object before the run starts.
options.explanation: The run context is for app state you already have. The reason is decided by the model at handoff time, so it cannot be set before the run.

options.text: Rename the handoff tool to include the priority with `tool_name_override`.
options.explanation: A tool name is fixed when you define it. It cannot carry a different priority for each customer.

options.text: Register one refund handoff per priority level and let the model choose.
options.explanation: One handoff per destination is for different specialists. Splitting one agent by priority adds routing surface and still logs no reason.

questions.prompt: Security moves the shop to server-managed history. How do you keep triage history away from the refund agent?

options.text: Keep the same `input_filter` on the refund handoff and test it again.
options.explanation: The docs say server-managed conversations do not support handoff input filters, so the filter would not apply.

options.text: Turn on `nest_handoff_history` so the history is summarized for it.
options.explanation: The docs say nested history changes how the transcript is shown. It does not redact sensitive data.

options.text: Start a separate run with chosen input, and do not reuse the old id.
options.explanation: Right. The docs say to use a separate run with explicitly selected input, and not to reuse the original `conversation_id` or `previous_response_id`.

options.text: Drop the filter and tell the refund agent to ignore internal notes.
options.explanation: A prompt cannot hide data the agent already received. The notes would still be in its input.
